newsitem.title: USA: Cumberland Cty, N.C., to vote on $98 million GOs.
newsitem.headline: Cumberland Cty, N.C., to vote on $98 million GOs.

text.p: North Carolina's Cumberland County Commission has approved a referendum on a $98 million general obligation bond issue for schools, the Observer-Times said Tuesday.
The commission approved the proposal in a 5-2 vote Monday but did not set a referendum date.

Commissioner Ed Melvin, who voted against the proposal, failed to persuade the board to limit the bond issue to $68 million. Melvin said debt service on the bonds, combined with existing debt and capital projects, could force the county to raise its ad valorem tax rate by 40 cents, to $1.10 per $100 of assessed value.
The commission also voted 6-1 to encourage large cities and counties to lobby the legislature for a one-cent increase in sales taxes to pay for school construction.
